name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
description: A large-scale supervised fine-tuning dataset for training reasoning models across math, code, and science domains. The dataset contains 1.2 million question-answer pairs with long-form reasoning traces generated by teacher models.
citeAs: Guha, E., Marten, R., Keh, S., et al. (2025). Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2506.04178v2.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed through a systematic pipeline involving: (1) sourcing questions from existing datasets and generating new questions, (2) mixing questions from top-performing sources, (3) filtering questions using LLM-based methods, (4) deduplicating questions, (5) generating multiple answers per question using teacher models, and (6) selecting the best teacher model. Questions were sourced from math (OpenMath-2-Math), code (CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning), and science (StackExchange Physics, Organic Chemistry PDFs) domains.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from multiple origins: (1) Existing datasets including OpenMath-2-Math, CodeGolf from StackExchange, OpenCodeReasoning, StackExchange Physics, and organic chemistry textbooks; (2) Semi-synthetic questions generated from seed data like CommonCrawl, FineWeb, and AutoMathText using LLMs; (3) Fully synthetic questions generated by LLMs with minimal seed material. The dataset covers 27 code question sources, 21 math sources, and 14 science sources.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions underwent several manipulation steps: (1) Mixing - selecting top 1-2 high-quality sources rather than diverse mixing; (2) Filtering - using LLM-based difficulty ratings and response length filtering with GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1 models; (3) Deduplication - exact match deduplication for math and science, no deduplication for code; (4) Multiple sampling - generating 16 answers per question from teacher models.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The preprocessing pipeline consisted of six stages: (1) Question sourcing from 62 total sources across domains; (2) Question mixing by selecting top 1-2 performing sources; (3) Question filtering using LLM-based methods (difficulty-based for code, response length-based for math and science); (4) Question deduplication using Indel similarity metric with 75% threshold; (5) Answer generation with 16x sampling per question; (6) Teacher model selection (QwQ-32B). Decontamination was performed against evaluation benchmarks using both Indel similarity (75% threshold) and 13-gram matching.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers and reasoning traces were generated by teacher models (primarily QwQ-32B, with initial experiments using DeepSeek-R1). For each question, 16 independent responses were sampled from the teacher model. The teacher models generated long-form reasoning traces (up to 32,768 tokens) enclosed in <think> and </think> tags, followed by final answers. Sampling used temperature=0.7, top_p=1.0.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Teacher model inference was performed using custom infrastructure on H100 and GH200 GPU nodes. Annotation required 22,000 H100 GPU hours on 16 1xNvidia GH200 nodes for the full dataset.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Multiple answer filtering strategies were tested including majority consensus, GPT verification, FastText classification, and length-based selection. Experiments showed that no filtering strategy significantly outperformed using all generated samples, so answer filtering was not applied in the final pipeline. The study found that 16x sampling per question provided better scaling than annotating more unique questions.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B (primary teacher model), DeepSeek-R1 (initial experiments), GPT-4o-mini (question generation and filtering), GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-4.1-nano (response length filtering), Phi-4-Reasoning-Plus (teacher model experiments)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is part of the OpenThoughts project with multiple generations released. OpenThoughts3-1.2M is the third major release following OpenThoughts-114K and OpenThoughts2-1M. All datasets and models are available on openthoughts.ai and Hugging Face. The project involves continuous experimentation and improvement of data recipes.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to democratize reasoning model development by creating open-source datasets and sharing systematic findings about data curation. Safety analysis revealed that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data degrades pre-existing safety alignment, with OpenThinker3-7B showing a 55.5% harmfulness rate on Harmbench compared to 14.5% for the base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model. The authors acknowledge the challenge of balancing safety and utility in reasoning models.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses on math, code, and science reasoning domains, which may not generalize to other reasoning tasks. Question sources are primarily from English-language competitive programming, mathematics competitions, and academic materials. The study found that models trained on this data show strong performance fluctuations on simple problem variations (Alice in Wonderland evaluation), indicating generalization deficits despite improved average performance.
rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) The dataset does not explore reinforcement learning data or curriculum learning approaches; (2) Pipeline choices optimized for overall average performance rather than domain-specific optimization; (3) Limited exploration of cross-domain transfer effects when domains are mixed; (4) Unclear whether performance plateaus or enables weak-to-strong generalization as student models approach teacher performance; (5) Some benchmarks show saturation (AMC23, MATH500) while others do not respond to scale (HLE); (6) Safety degradation compared to base models; (7) Generalization deficits on structure-preserving problem variations.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of reasoning models. Primary use case is training 7B-scale language models to develop reasoning capabilities across math, code, and science domains. The resulting OpenThinker3-7B model achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-data 7B models: 53% on AIME 2025, 51% on LiveCodeBench 06/24-01/25, and 54% on GPQA Diamond. The dataset enables research into reasoning model development, data curation strategies, and scaling laws for reasoning capabilities.
